name: dpik
title: Select a Bandwidth for Kernel Density Estimation

origin.description: Uses direct plug-in methodology to select the bandwidth of a kernel density estimate.
origin.usage:
dpik(x, scalest = "minim", level = 2L, kernel = "normal",
     canonical = FALSE, gridsize = 401L, range.x = range(x),
     truncate = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector containing the sample on which the kernel density estimate is to be constructed.

arguments.name: scalest
arguments.text: Estimate of scale: "stdev", "iqr" (interquartile range divided by 1.349), or "minim" (the smaller of those two).

arguments.name: level
arguments.text: Number of levels of functional estimation used in the plug-in rule.

arguments.name: canonical
arguments.text: If TRUE, canonically scaled kernels are used.

arguments.name: gridsize
arguments.text: Number of equally spaced points used in the binned functional approximation.

arguments.name: range.x
arguments.text: Minimum and maximum values of x at which to compute the estimate. The default is the data range.

arguments.name: truncate
arguments.text: If TRUE, data outside range.x are ignored.

origin.details: Unknown functionals in the expression for the asymptotically optimal bandwidth are replaced by kernel estimates. The normal distribution provides the initial estimate.

translation.description: Uses direct plug-in methodology to select the bandwidth of a kernel density estimate.
translation.usage:
dpik(x, scalest="minim", level=2, kernel="normal",
     canonical=False, gridsize=401, range_x=None,
     truncate=True)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: One-dimensional numeric sample on which the kernel density estimate is to be constructed.

arguments.name: scalest
arguments.text: Estimate of scale: "stdev", "iqr" (interquartile range divided by 1.349), or "minim" (the smaller of those two).

arguments.name: level
arguments.text: Number of levels of functional estimation used in the plug-in rule. An integer from 0 to 5. The default is 2.

arguments.name: canonical
arguments.text: If true, canonically scaled kernels are used.

arguments.name: gridsize
arguments.text: Number of equally spaced points used in the binned functional approximation.

arguments.name: range_x
arguments.text: The two endpoints at which to compute the estimate. This is range.x in R. None uses the minimum and maximum data values.

arguments.name: truncate
arguments.text: If true, data outside range_x are ignored.

translation.details: Unknown functionals in the expression for the asymptotically optimal bandwidth are replaced by kernel estimates from bkfe. Bin counts come from the Rust crate linbin. The normal distribution provides the initial estimate.
translation.example:
from mass import geyser
from kernsmooth import bkde, dpik
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = geyser["duration"]
h = dpik(x)
est = bkde(x, bandwidth=h)
plt.plot(est["x"], est["y"])
